sketch:
As in \cite{KLO14, CHL19, CV25}, the strategy is to study the distribution of the ratios of sizes of certain Selmer groups, and prove that they satisfy an analog of the celebrated Erd\H{o}s--Kac theorem \cite{EK40}. The key new ingredient is a systematic approach to counting elliptic curves over arbitrary number fields having a prescribed torsion subgroup and satisfying prescribed local conditions, achieved by extending previous work \cite{Phi24+}.

More concretely (per the paper outline): one (i) studies ratios of certain Selmer groups and relates them to ratios of certain Tamagawa numbers (Section \ref{sec:Selmer_ratios}); (ii) extends results of \cite{Phi24+} to count elliptic curves over number fields with prescribed torsion and prescribed local conditions (Section \ref{sec:local_conditions}, Proposition \ref{prop:elliptic_count_general}); (iii) proves that the logarithms of ratios of sizes of certain Selmer groups are normally distributed (an Erd\H{o}s--Kac type statement) (Section \ref{sec:Selmer_distribution}, Theorem \ref{thm:selmer_erdos_kac_prime}); and (iv) uses this to prove the main result (noted there as Theorem \ref{thm:main2}).

mcq.question: Suppose that $X_1(M,MN)$ has genus zero and that $p$ is a prime divisor of $MN$. Let $\cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)$ be the relevant family of elliptic curves over $K$ of height bounded by $B$. As $B\to\infty$, what is the strongest asymptotic lower bound one can assert for the limsup of the average of $\#\Sel_p(E)$ over $E\in\cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)$, and what additional conclusion holds if $(M,N,p,\sG_{MN}(K))$ avoids the listed exceptional tuples?

correct_choice.label: A
correct_choice.text:
There exists an explicit constant $\theta$ depending only on $M$, $N$, $K$, and $p$ such that
\[
\limsup_{B\to\infty} \frac{1}{\# \cE_{(M,MN)}(B; K)} \sum_{E\in \cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)} \# \Sel_p(E) \gg \log(B)^{\theta}.
\]
If moreover
\[
(M,N, p, \sG_{MN}(K))\not\in 
\begin{Bmatrix}
(1,5, 5, ({\mathbb Z}/5{\mathbb Z})^\times), (1,7, 7, \{1,4,7\}\ \text{or}\ ({\mathbb Z}/7{\mathbb Z})^\times),
(1, 10, 5, ({\mathbb Z}/10{\mathbb Z})^\times), (2,2, 2, \ast), (2, 6, 3, ({\mathbb Z}/6{\mathbb Z})^\times),
(3,3, 3, \ast), (3,6, 3, \ast), (4,4,2,({\mathbb Z}/4{\mathbb Z})^\times), (5,5,5,\ast)
\end{Bmatrix},
\]
then $\theta>0$, and in particular the average size of the $p$-Selmer group is unbounded as $B\to\infty$.

choices.label: B
choices.text:
There exists an explicit constant $\theta$ depending only on $M$, $N$, $K$, and $p$ such that
\[
\liminf_{B\to\infty} \frac{1}{\# \cE_{(M,MN)}(B; K)} \sum_{E\in \cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)} \# \Sel_p(E) \gg \log(B)^{\theta}.
\]
If moreover the tuple $(M,N,p,\sG_{MN}(K))$ avoids the listed exceptional cases, then one can take $\theta>0$ and the same lower bound holds with $\liminf$ in place of $\limsup$, so the average size of $\Sel_p(E)$ diverges.

choices.label: C
choices.text:
There exists a constant $\theta$ depending only on $M$, $N$, $K$, and $p$ such that
\[
\limsup_{B\to\infty} \frac{1}{\# \cE_{(M,MN)}(B; K)} \sum_{E\in \cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)} \# \Sel_p(E) \gg \log(B)^{\theta}.
\]
If moreover $(M,N,p,\sG_{MN}(K))$ avoids the listed exceptional tuples, then the average size of the $p$-Selmer group is unbounded as $B\to\infty$.

choices.label: D
choices.text:
There exists an explicit constant $\theta$ depending only on $M$, $N$, $K$, and $p$ such that
\[
\limsup_{B\to\infty} \frac{1}{\# \cE_{(M,MN)}(B; K)} \sum_{E\in \cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)} \# \Sel_p(E) \gg (\log\log B)^{\theta}.
\]
If moreover $(M,N,p,\sG_{MN}(K))$ avoids the listed exceptional tuples, then $\theta>0$, implying that the average size of the $p$-Selmer group is unbounded.

choices.label: E
choices.text:
There exists an explicit constant $\theta$ depending only on $M$, $N$, $K$, and $p$ such that
\[
\limsup_{B\to\infty} \frac{1}{\# \cE_{(M,MN)}(B; K)} \sum_{E\in \cE_{(M,MN)}(B;K)} \# \Sel_p(E) \gg \log(B)^{\theta}.
\]
If moreover $(M,N,p,\sG_{MN}(K))$ avoids the listed exceptional tuples, then $\theta$ is positive for every prime $p$ (not necessarily dividing $MN$), and hence the average size of $\Sel_p(E)$ is unbounded as $B\to\infty$.

theorem.content:
[Expression and asymptotics for the partition function]
\label{thm:F_ell_main}
We have the exact expression
	\[
	F_\ell
	=
	\int_{\gamma_-}^{\gamma_+}
	\rho(y) y^{\ell} \mathrm{d}y,
    \quad \ell\geq 1,
	\] 
where 
    \[
    \rho(y) =  
    \frac{2^{-\theta - 1/2}}{\pi\theta(\gamma_+\!-\gamma_-)}  (\gamma_+-y)^{1-\theta} \bigg( \Big( \sqrt{2\gamma_+ - \gamma_- -y} + \sqrt{y-\gamma_-}\Big)^{2\theta} - \Big( \sqrt{2\gamma_+ - \gamma_- -y} - \sqrt{y-\gamma_-}\Big)^{2\theta}\bigg),
    \]
    and 
    \[
\gamma_+ = 2^{3/2} \cos\left( \frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right) \quad \text{and} \quad \gamma_+-\gamma_- = \frac{2^{3/2}}{\theta} \sin\left(\frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right).
\]
theorem.label: thm:F_ell_main

ref_dict.thm:F_ell_main:
\begin{Thm}[Expression and asymptotics for the partition function]
\label{thm:F_ell_main}
We have the exact expression
	\[
	F_\ell
	=
	\int_{\gamma_-}^{\gamma_+}
	\rho(y) y^{\ell} \mathrm{d}y,
    \quad \ell\geq 1,
	\] 
where 
    \[
    \rho(y) =  
    \frac{2^{-\theta - 1/2}}{\pi\theta(\gamma_+\!-\gamma_-)}  (\gamma_+-y)^{1-\theta} \bigg( \Big( \sqrt{2\gamma_+ - \gamma_- -y} + \sqrt{y-\gamma_-}\Big)^{2\theta} - \Big( \sqrt{2\gamma_+ - \gamma_- -y} - \sqrt{y-\gamma_-}\Big)^{2\theta}\bigg),
    \]
    and 
    \[
\gamma_+ = 2^{3/2} \cos\left( \frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right) \quad \text{and} \quad \gamma_+-\gamma_- = \frac{2^{3/2}}{\theta} \sin\left(\frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right).
\]
\end{Thm}

post_theorem_intro_text:
In particular, we deduce the following asymptotics.
\begin{Cor} \label{cor:asymp_F_ell_main}
    The partition function satisfies:
    \begin{equation} \label{eq:asymp_F_ell_main}
	F_\ell 
	\sim
	c \frac{\gamma_+^{\ell}}{\ell^{2-\theta}} \quad \text{as } \ell\to\infty,
	\end{equation}
	where $c =\frac{2^{\theta-1/2}}{\pi \theta} (\gamma_+-\gamma_-)^{\theta-1} \gamma_+^{1-\theta} \Gamma(2-\theta)$, and $\gamma_-$ and $\gamma_+$ are as above.
\end{Cor}

\noindent Observe that the form of the asymptotic \eqref{eq:asymp_F_ell_main} is characteristic of the critical (in fact, more precisely, \textbf{non-generic critical} according to the terminology of \cite{BBG12}) phase of the loop-$O(n)$ model, with the exponent $2-\theta$ interpolating between $3/2$ and $2$ (see e.g.\ \cite[Section 5]{BBG12}). More precisely, it lies in the so-called \emph{dense} phase of the model, where loops are conjectured to be non-simple and to touch each other in the scaling limit. 

Our second main result determines the exact tail exponents for the size of typical loops and clusters in the original FK$(q)$-weighted planar map model. This sharpens the main theorem of \cite{berestycki2017critical} by identifying the previously implicit $\ell^{o(1)}$ factor as a true constant {(a similar result can also be deduced from  \cite{gwynne2019scaling}, with the $\ell^{o(1)}$ term identified as a slowly varying function)}. We denote by $\mathfrak{L}$ and $\mathfrak{K}$ the typical loop and (filled-in) cluster in the \emph{infinite} FK$(q)$ planar map. These correspond to the local limit of a uniformly chosen loop or (filled-in) cluster in a finite FK$(q)$ map of size $k$, and then sending $k$ to infinity, see \cite[Theorem 1.1]{berestycki2017critical}.
We define the perimeter $|\mathfrak{L}|$ of the loop $\mathfrak{L}$ as the number of triangles it crosses, and the perimeter $|\partial \mathfrak{K}|$ of the cluster as the degree of its external face, see \cref{sec:typ_cluster} for more precise definitions.

\begin{Thm}[Exponents for loops and clusters]
\label{thm:exp_main}
    We have the following tail asymptotics: as $\ell\to\infty$,
    \[
    \mathbb{P}(|\partial \mathfrak{K}| = \ell) \sim \frac{C}{\ell^{3-2\theta}}
    \quad \text{and} \quad 
    \mathbb{P}(|\mathfrak{L}| = \ell) \sim \frac{C'}{\ell^{3-2\theta}},
    \]
    where $C$ and $C'$ are positive constants.
\end{Thm}

Our strategy to prove the above two theorems is the following. First, we make some connections between the gasket decomposition approach and Sheffield's hamburger-cheeseburger bijection. This allows us to express the partition function (up to an explicit factor) as a hitting time probability for the burger walk. We use this information in both directions, as it will enable us to: (a) rigorously justify the missing ansatz in the gasket decomposition approach, and then deduce the exact expression of the partition from there; (b) feed this information back into the burger walks to derive exact asymptotics for the hitting times, and thus for loops and clusters.

The paper is organised as follows. \cref{sec:prelim} is dedicated to preliminaries on self-dual FK planar maps, the $O(n)$ model and the Mullin--Bernardi--Sheffield bijection. In \cref{sec:self_dual_critical}, we make some connections between Sheffield's hamburger-cheeseburger walk and the gasket decomposition of Borot, Bouttier and Guitter. In particular, this allows us to prove an ansatz on the \emph{cut} of the associated resolvent function using solely hamburger-cheeseburger arguments: we will derive an explicit formula for the right endpoint $\gamma_+$ of the cut.  We will then use this information in \cref{sec:resolvents}, where we solve the resolvent equation for the fully packed $O(n)$ model on triangulations, thus proving \cref{thm:F_ell_main}. Finally, in \cref{sec:loop-clusters}, we come back to the hamburger-cheeseburger model and deduce \cref{thm:exp_main} by plugging back the information on the partition function.

We stress that this dictionary has been used in \cite{da2025scaling}, which concerns the critical case $q=4$ (equivalently, $n=2$). In that case, the authors prove the analogue of \cref{thm:F_ell_main} by directing solving the gasket decomposition equation (without any extra input) and then deduce the scaling limit of FK$(4)$-weighted planar maps in the peanosphere sense, resolving the remaining open regime in Sheffield's work \cite{sheffield2016quantum}.

mcq.question:
Fix a parameter \(\theta\) and define numbers \(\gamma_+\) and \(\gamma_-\) by
\[
\gamma_+ = 2^{3/2}\cos\left(\frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right),\qquad \gamma_+-\gamma_- = \frac{2^{3/2}}{\theta}\sin\left(\frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right).
\]
For an integer \(\ell\ge 1\), what is the strongest exact integral representation for \(F_\ell\) in terms of an explicit function \(\rho(y)\) supported on \([\gamma_-,\gamma_+]\)?

choices.label: C
choices.text:
For every integer \(\ell\ge 1\),
\[
F_\ell=\int_{\gamma_-}^{\gamma_+}\rho(y)\,y^{\ell}\,\mathrm{d}y,
\]
for some explicit density \(\rho(y)\) supported on \([\gamma_-,\gamma_+]\), where
\[
\gamma_+ = 2^{3/2}\cos\left(\frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right),\qquad \gamma_+-\gamma_- = \frac{2^{3/2}}{\theta}\sin\left(\frac{\pi\theta}{2}\right).
\]

post_theorem_intro_text:
\begin{proof}
We synthesize the results established in the subsequent sections.

\textbf{Part 1 (Topological Collapse):} For $\epsilon=0$, by the Dimensional Inflation Law (Corollary~\ref{cor:inflation_law}), $d_{\rm M} = d_{\rm A} - 2$. For $\epsilon \neq 0$, $G_{P_\epsilon}$ is trivial. By the Generalized Symmetry Reduction Theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:generalized_symmetry_reduction}), the roots are isolated ($d_{\rm M}=0$). The discontinuity follows (Proposition~\ref{prop:collapse}).

\textbf{Part 2 (Algebraic Singularity):} The tangent space $T_x V_0$ is related to $\Ker(J_{P_0}(x))$. The rank deficiency follows from the positive dimension of the manifold (Theorem~\ref{thm:jacobian_singularity}).

\textbf{Part 3 (Dynamical Retraction):} The potential $\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)$ is real-analytic and coercive. The Lojasiewicz gradient inequality \cite{lojasiewicz1963propriete} guarantees convergence of the gradient flow (Theorem~\ref{thm:deformation_retract}). The timescale scaling $T_{\rm collapse} \propto \epsilon^{-2}$ is derived from the quadratic scaling of the restricted potential (Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse_timescale}) and the generic Lojasiewicz exponent (Proposition~\ref{prop:lojasiewicz_exponent}).

\textbf{Part 4 (Thermodynamic Phase Transition):} We define the Gibbs measure (Definition~\ref{def:gibbs_measure}) and the alignment order parameter $m(\epsilon, T)$ (Definition~\ref{def:order_parameter}). In the limit $T \to 0$, the measure concentrates on $V_\epsilon$. For $\epsilon=0$, symmetry implies $m(0, 0) = 1/(d_{\rm A}-1)$. For $\epsilon \neq 0$, the Localization Theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:algebraic_alignment}) implies alignment, $m(\epsilon, 0) = 1$. The discontinuity characterizes the phase transition (Theorem~\ref{thm:phase_transition}).
\end{proof}

mcq.question: Let \(\mathbb{A}\in\{\mathbb{H},\mathbb{O}\}\) and let \(P_0(x)\) be a central polynomial over \(\mathbb{A}\) whose root variety \(V_0=Z(P_0)\) contains a non-real manifold of dimension \(d_{\rm M}>0\). Let \(P_\epsilon(x)\) be a generically non-central analytic deformation with root variety \(V_\epsilon=Z(P_\epsilon)\), and set \(d_{\rm A}=\dim(\mathbb{A})\). As \(\epsilon\to 0\) (and, for the statistical statement, as \((\epsilon,T)\to(0,0)\)), which strongest combined limiting/asymptotic description is justified for the geometry, Jacobian rank, gradient-flow dynamics, and thermodynamic order parameter?

correct_choice.label: A
correct_choice.text: One of the remaining options is correct, but a stronger result can be proven.

choices.label: B
choices.text: (i) The Hausdorff dimension of \(V_\epsilon\) converges continuously to that of \(V_0\) as \(\epsilon\to 0\), but the topology changes (e.g. \(V_\epsilon\) becomes a finite set for \(\epsilon\neq 0\)). (ii) The Jacobian of the central fiber satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(J_{P_0}(x))=d_{\rm A}\) for \(x\in V_0\) (i.e. no rank deficiency). (iii) With \(\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)=\|P_\epsilon(x)\|^2\), the gradient flow \(\dot x=-\nabla\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)\) still yields a deformation retract \(V_0\to V_\epsilon\), and the collapse timescale obeys critical slowing down \(T_{\rm collapse}\propto \epsilon^{-2}\). (iv) The order parameter \(m(\epsilon,T)\) extends continuously to \((\epsilon,T)=(0,0)\).

choices.label: C
choices.text: (i) For a generically non-central analytic deformation, the solution set \(V_\epsilon=Z(P_\epsilon)\) is generically zero-dimensional for \(\epsilon\neq 0\) while \(V_0\) contains a positive-dimensional non-real manifold, so the Hausdorff dimension changes discontinuously at \(\epsilon=0\). (ii) On the central fiber \(V_0\), the Jacobian \(J_{P_0}(x)\) is singular for all \(x\in V_0\). (iii) For \(\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)=\|P_\epsilon(x)\|^2\), the gradient flow \(\dot x=-\nabla\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)\) converges and defines a deformation retract from \(V_0\) onto \(V_\epsilon\). (iv) In the zero-temperature limit, an alignment order parameter can exhibit a discontinuity at \((\epsilon,T)=(0,0)\).

choices.label: D
choices.text: (i) The Hausdorff dimension of \(V_\epsilon\) changes discontinuously at \(\epsilon=0\). (ii) The central fiber has Jacobian rank deficiency \(\operatorname{rank}(J_{P_0}(x))=d_{\rm A}-d_{\rm M}\). (iii) With \(\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)=\|P_\epsilon(x)\|^2\), the gradient flow \(\dot x=-\nabla\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)\) realizes the collapse as a deformation retract, but the critical slowing down is linear: \(T_{\rm collapse}\propto \epsilon^{-1}\). (iv) The order parameter \(m(\epsilon,T)\) is discontinuous at \((\epsilon,T)=(0,0)\).

choices.label: E
choices.text: (i) The Hausdorff dimension of \(V_\epsilon\) changes discontinuously at \(\epsilon=0\). (ii) The central fiber \(V_0\) is characterized by \(\operatorname{rank}(J_{P_0}(x))=d_{\rm A}-d_{\rm M}\). (iii) For \(\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)=\|P_\epsilon(x)\|^2\), the gradient flow \(\dot x=-\nabla\mathcal{V}_\epsilon(x)\) yields a deformation retract and the collapse timescale satisfies the stronger universal law \(T_{\rm collapse}\propto \epsilon^{-2}\) for all analytic perturbations (including non-generic ones), with no dependence on any \L ojasiewicz exponent. (iv) In the Gibbs ensemble at temperature \(T\), the order parameter satisfies \(m(0,0)=0\) by symmetry and \(m(\epsilon,0)=1\) for \(\epsilon\neq 0\), hence is discontinuous at \((\epsilon,T)=(0,0)\).
